review.dynamicFileAccess: Reviewed the existing LoTKT/dist/LoTKT_Lua-built.w3x input on 2026-10-03: 60,727,110 map bytes and 8,142,502 Lua bytes. Its single Preloader reference is File.readPreload(self.filename). The two FileIO_Read callers supply the local constant 클랜지키기.txt; the save writer supplies the same filename; FileIO.Init supplies FileTester.pld. No other File.open callers select a filename. The two dynamic _G indexes belong to InventoryNativeCompat.Resolve, whose callers supply seven explicit inventory native names. The compiled MapInitializer registers 31 literal model paths for PreloadConfiguredFiles. None of these reviewed paths select a cleanup candidate.
review.objectAndImportReferences: Read all 909 named entries in this exact input. Outside the four deletion candidates, the only candidate filename reference was the custom-path lotkt-object-history.json record in war3map.imp; cleanup removes this inventory record. Parsed the ten unit, ability, item, buff and upgrade base/skin object payloads: 8,100 records and 100,767 string fields contained no candidate filename references. The history hash and all twelve payload hashes in lotkt-object-receipt.json matched the corresponding input bytes. Build source inspection confirms that history and receipt are consumed by object reconciliation/adoption tools and are not loaded by the map Lua.
review.limitations: This is an explicit dependency review for one exact input, not a static proof or Warcraft III game validation. The four FileIO/save/native-compat modules were compared with their embedded compiled source; this does not claim that the entire map reflects the latest LoTKT checkout. External save payloads are assumed to follow the existing FileIO tooltip-data format; modified external scripts, injected runtime code and add-ons are outside this review. Unnamed files are preserved. Any change to the input map or Lua invalidates this contract and requires a fresh dependency review. Keep the editable original for World Editor, rebuilding and object adoption; use cleanup only on a separate distribution copy. Gameplay, saves and multiplayer still need game testing.

files.reason: Editor trigger definitions are retained in the editable original. This reviewed Lua map executes the already assembled root war3map.lua, and its reviewed file/resource access paths do not read the trigger definition file.
evidence: LoTKT/build/build-lua.mjs:192-235 preserves editor main/config, appends LoTKTLua.Start and the source bundle, and replaces root war3map.lua.
Reviewed compiled war3map.lua:218901 File.readPreload; 217833 and 217864 save reads; 218991 FileTester.pld initialization.
All ten base/skin object payloads and the other decoded named input entries contain no war3map.wtg filename reference.

files.reason: Custom editor trigger data is retained in the editable original. This exact input contains a 14-byte war3map.wct and the complete runtime script in root war3map.lua; reviewed runtime file/resource access does not read war3map.wct.
evidence: LoTKT/build/build-lua.mjs:192-235 emits the complete executable code into war3map.lua rather than reading wct at game runtime.
Reviewed compiled war3map.lua FileIO and model preloading call paths select save files and model paths, never war3map.wct.
All ten base/skin object payloads and the other decoded named input entries contain no war3map.wct filename reference.

files.reason: Build-only object reconciliation/adoption history; removing it from this distribution copy does not remove the actual object payloads. It remains in the editable/build input, and is not needed by the reviewed game Lua.
evidence: LoTKT/build/object-history.mjs:5,14-35,76-151 generates the metadata, registers its custom import path for editor retention, and uses it to reconcile object fields during builds.
LoTKT/build/object-history.mjs:155-176 consumes the history during object adoption; LoTKT/build/build-lua.mjs:235 inserts it as a separate map entry.

The 24,957,893-byte input history matches receipt.historyHash. No compiled Lua or object/skin string field references its filename; the sole external named-entry reference is its removable war3map.imp row.

files.reason: Build-only provenance and payload checksums for object adoption. The game consumes the actual Lua/object/resource payloads, which cleanup preserves, and the reviewed game Lua does not load this receipt.
evidence: LoTKT/build/object-history.mjs:155-179 reads the receipt in adoptionEntries and generates source/history/payload hashes in objectReceipt.
LoTKT/build/build-lua.mjs:235 adds the receipt as a separate build result entry.
The input receipt matches the history and all twelve recorded payload hashes. No compiled Lua, object/skin string field or other decoded named input entry references lotkt-object-receipt.json.
